academic_translation: Moreover, Subhūti, whatever is the perfection of patience of the Tathāgata, that itself is no perfection.
translation: Also, Subhuti, whatever is the perfect patience of the Thus-Gone One, that itself is no perfection."

academic_translation: Why is that? Subhūti, at the time when the king of Kaliṅga severed my limbs and minor limbs, neither the perception of a self, nor the perception of a sentient being, nor the perception of a life-force, nor the perception of a person arose in me, and
translation: Why is that? Subhuti, when the king of Kalinga cut off my limbs, I did not have the idea of a self. I did not have the idea of a living being, the idea of a life, or the idea of a person, and

academic_translation: because I had no perception whatsoever, and it was not the case that I was without perception.
translation: because I had no idea at all, and it was not that I was without an idea.

academic_translation: Why is that? Subhūti, if at that time the perception of a self had arisen in me, then at that time the perception of malice would also have arisen, and
translation: Why is that? Subhuti, if I had the idea of a self at that time, I would also have had the idea of a wish to harm, and

academic_translation: because if the perception of a sentient being, the perception of a life-force, or the perception of a person had arisen, then at that time the perception of malice would also have arisen.
translation: because if I had the idea of a living being, the idea of a life, or the idea of a person, I would also have had the idea of a wish to harm.

academic_translation: Subhūti, I remember that in the past, when I was the sage called Kṣāntivādin for five hundred lifetimes, even at that time the perception of a self did not arise in me.
translation: Subhuti, I remember that in the past I was the sage called Speaker of Patience for five hundred lifetimes. Even then, I did not have the idea of a self.

academic_translation: Neither the perception of a sentient being, nor the perception of a life-force, nor the perception of a person arose.
translation: I did not have the idea of a living being, the idea of a life, or the idea of a person.

academic_translation: Therefore, Subhūti, a bodhisattva great being, having completely abandoned all perceptions,
translation: Therefore, Subhuti, a great awakening hero should let go of every idea.

academic_translation: should generate the mind for unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening.
translation: They should set the mind on the highest, complete awakening.

academic_translation: They should generate the mind without abiding in form.
translation: They should set the mind without staying in a shape.

academic_translation: They should generate the mind without abiding in sound, smell, taste, or tangible objects.
translation: They should set the mind without staying in a sound, a smell, a taste, or a thing that is touched.

academic_translation: One should generate the mind without abiding in phenomena.
translation: They should set the mind without staying in a thing.

academic_translation: One should generate the mind without abiding even in non-phenomena.
translation: They should set the mind without staying even in a non-thing.

academic_translation: One should generate the mind without abiding in anything at all.
translation: You should set the mind without staying in anything at all.

academic_translation: Why is that? Because whatever is an abiding is itself without abiding.
translation: Why is that? Because whatever is staying is itself without staying.

academic_translation: Therefore, the Tathāgata has spoken thus: "A bodhisattva should practice generosity without abiding in anything at all."
translation: That is why the Thus-Gone One said: "An awakening hero should practice giving without staying in anything at all."

academic_translation: Furthermore, Subhūti, a bodhisattva should completely relinquish generosity in this way for the benefit of all sentient beings.
translation: Also, Subhuti, an awakening hero should completely let go of giving in this way to help all living beings.

academic_translation: Whatever is the perception as a sentient being is itself a non-perception.
translation: Whatever is the idea of a living being is itself an absence of ideas.

academic_translation: Those very sentient beings that the Tathāgata has spoken of as "all sentient beings" are themselves non-existent.
translation: Those living beings that the Thus-Gone One called "all living beings" do not exist.

academic_translation: Why is that? Subhūti, the Tathāgata speaks authentically, speaks truthfully, and speaks in accordance with suchness,
translation: Why is that? Subhuti, the Thus-Gone One speaks what is real. He speaks the truth. He speaks according to the way things are.

academic_translation: because the Tathāgata does not speak falsely.
translation: This is because the Thus-Gone One does not speak falsely.

academic_translation: Furthermore, Subhūti, in whatever phenomenon the Tathāgata has fully awakened to or taught, there is neither truth nor falsehood.
translation: Also, Subhuti, in whatever thing the Thus-Gone One is fully awake to or teaches, there is neither truth nor a lie.

academic_translation: Subhūti, it is like this: for example, just as a person with sight who has entered into darkness sees nothing at all, in the same way should one view a bodhisattva who completely gives generosity having fallen into entities.
translation: Subhuti, it is like this. Imagine a person with sight who walks into the dark and sees nothing at all. You should view an awakening hero who practices giving while caught up in real objects in the exact same way.

academic_translation: Furthermore, Subhūti, it is like this: for example, when dawn breaks and the sun rises, a person with sight sees various forms; in the same way should one view a bodhisattva who completely gives generosity without having fallen into entities.
translation: Also, Subhuti, it is like this. When dawn breaks and the sun rises, a person with sight sees many forms. You should view an awakening hero who practices giving without getting caught up in objects in the exact same way.

academic_translation: Furthermore, Subhūti, whatever sons of noble family or daughters of noble family take up this Dharma discourse, hold it, keep it, read it, completely master it, and extensively and authentically teach it to others, those are known by the Tathāgata, and are seen by the Tathāgata,

locked_terms.use: son of a good family or daughter of a good family

translation: Also, Subhuti, think of any son of a good family or daughter of a good family who takes up this lesson on the teaching. They hold it, keep it, read it, and master it completely. They teach it to others widely and truly. The Thus-Gone One knows them, and the Thus-Gone One sees them.

academic_translation: all those sentient beings will generate an immeasurable mass of merit.
translation: All those living beings will create a pile of stored-up goodness that cannot be measured.

academic_translation: Moreover, Subhūti, if a man or a woman were to completely give away bodies as numerous as the grains of sand in the Gaṅgā river during the morning, and were also to completely give away bodies as numerous as the grains of sand in the Gaṅgā river during midday and during the afternoon, compared to completely giving away bodies in this manner for many hundred-thousands of myriads of millions of eons,
translation: Also, Subhuti, a man or woman might give away their bodies. They might give away as many bodies as there are sand grains in the Ganges River in the morning. They might do the same at midday and in the afternoon. Imagine they gave away their bodies like this for many millions of long ages.

academic_translation: if someone, having heard this Dharma discourse, does not abandon it, they would on that basis generate much more merit, countless and immeasurable. What need is there to mention someone who writes it down, takes it up, holds it, keeps it, reads it, completely masters it, and extensively and correctly teaches it to others?
translation: But what if someone hears this lesson on the teaching and does not give it up? They will create much more stored-up goodness than that. It is countless and cannot be measured. What need is there to even mention someone who writes it down, takes it up, keeps it, reads it, masters it, and teaches it to others?

academic_translation: Furthermore, Subhūti, this Dharma discourse is inconceivable and incomparable.
translation: Also, Subhuti, this lesson on the teaching cannot be imagined. It cannot be compared to anything else.

academic_translation: Its ripening should also be known to be inconceivable.
translation: You should know that its ripening also cannot be imagined.

academic_translation: The Tathāgata has spoken this Dharma discourse for the sake of those sentient beings who have correctly entered the supreme vehicle, and for the sake of those sentient beings who have correctly entered the foremost vehicle.
translation: The Thus-Gone One spoke this lesson on the teaching for living beings who have rightly entered the best vehicle. He also spoke it for living beings who have rightly entered the best vehicle.

tibetan: གང་དག་ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྣམ་གྲངས་འདི་ལེན་པ་དང༌། འཛིན་པ་དང༌། འཆང་བ་དང༌། ཀློག་པ་དང༌། ཀུན་ཆུབ་པར་བྱེད་པ་དང༌། གཞན་དག་ལ་རྒྱ་ཆེར་ཡང་དག་པར་རབ་ཏུ་སྟོན་པ་དེ་དག་ནི་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པས་མཁྱེན། དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པས་གཟིགས་ཏེ།
academic_translation: The Tathāgata knows and the Tathāgata sees those who take up, hold, keep, read, master, and extensively and authentically teach this Dharma discourse to others;
translation: The Thus-Gone One knows and the Thus-Gone One sees those who take up, hold, keep, read, master, and widely and truly teach this lesson on the teaching to others.

academic_translation: all those sentient beings will be endowed with an immeasurable mass of merit,
translation: All those living beings will have a pile of stored-up goodness that cannot be measured.

academic_translation: they will be endowed with an inconceivable, incomparable, immeasurable, and limitless mass of merit,
translation: They will have a pile of stored-up goodness that cannot be imagined, matched, measured, or limited.

academic_translation: All those sentient beings will carry my awakening upon their shoulders.
translation: All those living beings will carry my awakening on their shoulders.

academic_translation: Why is that? Subhūti, this Dharma discourse cannot be heard by those who are inclined toward the inferior,
translation: Why is that? Subhuti, this lesson on the teaching cannot be heard by those who are drawn to the lesser,

academic_translation: nor by those who hold the view of a self, nor by those who hold the view of a sentient being, nor by those who hold the view of a life-force,
translation: nor by those who hold the view of a self, the view of a living being, or the view of a life.

academic_translation: and those who hold a view of a person are unable to listen to, take up, retain, read, or master it,
translation: And those who hold a view of a person cannot listen to it, take it up, remember it, read it, or master it,

academic_translation: because that is impossible.
translation: because that is impossible.

academic_translation: Moreover, Subhūti, any place where this sūtra is taught will become worthy of being venerated by the world with its gods, humans, and demigods.

locked_terms.use: world with its gods, people, and jealous gods

translation: Also, Subhuti, any place where this sacred text is taught will deserve respect. It will be honored by the world with its gods, humans, and jealous gods.
